title: Entropy-calibrated admission with attention-skip profiling
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We observe intermittent long tail latencies (~95-99th) on mixed-tenant continuous batching workloads. Root causes appear to be a combination of: (1) suboptimal kernel choices when attention sparsity increases during prefill-to-decode handoff, (2) admission decisions that treat per-request entropy the same as average token distributions, and (3) contention when small high-entropy requests coalesce with large low-entropy streams leading to kernel mismatches and stragglers. Goal: Build an entropy-calibrated admission controller that annotates requests with a lightweight entropy/complexity signal at enqueue time, use that signal to shape batches and select kernel variants (e.g., dense vs. sparse attention, fused kernels for short sequences), and introduce a transient attention-skip profiling pass to better predict kernel fit during prefill. This ticket covers research spikes, prototype admission logic, kernel hint propagation, and canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype that tags incoming requests with a 1-byte entropy heuristic and routes them through the new admission path
Batch shaping reduces 99th percentile latency by at least 20% on the mixed workload replay compared to mainline for the target model (gptx-8k-quant)
Kernel selector uses the entropy hint to prefer attention-optimized kernels when predicted benefit > 5% token-cost, and falls back gracefully
Automated e2e test harness that replays production traces with injected high-entropy bursts and asserts no regression at p50/p90 and measurable improvement at p99
Documentation + console dashboard panel displaying entropy distribution, admission decisions, and kernel-mapping heatmap for the canary cohort
implementation_plan: Spike (3d): implement a lightweight entropy heuristic in the request parser (char/token-level entropy estimate + source-length-normalized score)
Prototype (5d): plumb entropy hint through admission pipeline and batch-shaper; implement scoring function used by admission to split or coalesce batches
Kernel mapping (4d): extend kernel selector to consider entropy hint and attention-skip profiling results; add metrics for kernel-mismatch events
Profiling pass (3d): implement single-iteration attention-skip profiler during prefill warmup to collect early token sparsity signals (must be O(1) overhead per request on average)
Integration (4d): add canary flag, dashboard panels, and backpressure safeguards; run mixed-tenant replay and iterate on thresholds
Rollout (2d): staged canary to 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% with rollout checks and automatic rollback on SLO breach
risks: Entropy heuristic may be gamed or misleading for certain tokenizer behaviors (need validation across en, zh, code-text)
Profiling pass could add non-trivial overhead if not carefully amortized across long sequences
Kernel selector complexity growth — risk of rule explosion leading to harder maintainability
Interaction with autoscaling and Dedicated capacity policies could change observed benefits; need to test on Dedicated clusters
Possible customer impact during canary if thresholds are tuned incorrectly — mitigation by conservative defaults and circuit-breakers
testing_plan: Unit tests for entropy heuristic with synthetic token distributions
Microbenchmarks: kernel-run latency & throughput for attention-optimized vs baseline kernels across sequence lengths and sparsity levels
Replay tests: run 7-day production trace replays with high-entropy injection against mainline and prototype; collect p50/p90/p99 and per-token cost
A/B canary in staging then prod with SLO gates (latency & error rate) and automated rollback when gates violated
Chaos test: spike-simulated small high-entropy bursts while varying admission thresholds to validate stability
notes: Related research: compare to ENG-24199 adaptive-servo-kernel-ranking for kernel scoring logic and ENG-271828 continuous-adaptive-batch-sculptor for shaping heuristics
We must coordinate with Runtime Ops to expose new kernel-mismatch and entropy histograms to the Console tracing pipeline
Prototype should avoid adding more than 3% tail to p95 on low-entropy synthetic steady streams
We will instrument samples for model-quality regression; ensure no degradation in token-level outputs when different kernel chosen (determinism checks)
